result.topic_en: Euler lists the infinite double series of the form 1/(x^m (x+a)^n) to which the problem reduces, and begins summing them by decomposing each term into simpler partial fractions.
result.transcription:
SERIES SINGVLARES. 145
ad ſequentes ſeries infinitas reduci:
$+\frac{1}{1.2^n}+\frac{1}{2^m.3^n}+\frac{1}{3^m.4^n}+\text{etc.}+\frac{1}{1.2^m}+\frac{1}{2^n.3^m}+\frac{1}{3^n.4^m}+\text{etc.}$
$+\frac{1}{1.3^n}+\frac{1}{2^m.4^n}+\frac{1}{3^m.5^n}+\text{etc.}+\frac{1}{1.3^m}+\frac{1}{2^n.4^m}+\frac{1}{3^n.5^m}+\text{etc.}$
$+\frac{1}{1.4^n}+\frac{1}{2^m.5^n}+\frac{1}{3^m.6^n}+\text{etc.}+\frac{1}{1.4^m}+\frac{1}{2^n.5^m}+\frac{1}{3^n.6^m}+\text{etc.}$
$+\frac{1}{1.5^n}+\frac{1}{2^m.6^n}+\frac{1}{3^m.7^n}+\text{etc.}+\frac{1}{1.5^m}+\frac{1}{2^n.6^m}+\frac{1}{3^n.7^m}+\text{etc.}$
etc. etc.
totumque negotium iam hinc redit, vt ſingulae hae
ſeries commode ſummentur; quo ipſo vberrimus
campus aperitur peculiare ſerierum genus comple-
ctens, quod ob concinnitatem per ſe omni attentio-
ne dignum videtur, etiamſi cum inſtituto noſtro non
tam arcto vinculo eſſet connexum.
6. Hae autem ſummationes commodius inueſti-
gari nequeunt, quam ſingulos terminos, quorum
forma eſt $\frac{1}{x^m(x+a)^n}$, in fractiones ſimpliciores re-
ſoluendo. Per ea autem quae de hoc argumento in
Introductione ad Analyſin tradidi, patet, hanc fra-
ctionem in ſequentes diſcerpi:
$\frac{1}{a^n}\cdot\frac{1}{x^m}-\frac{n}{1.a^{n+1}}\cdot\frac{1}{x^{m-1}}+\frac{n(n+1)}{1.2\,a^{n+2}}\cdot\frac{1}{x^{m-2}}$
$-\frac{n(n+1)(n+2)}{1.2.3\,a^{n+3}}\cdot\frac{1}{x^{m-3}}+\text{etc.}$
Tom. XX. Nou. Comm. T $+$
